title: What If You Fell Into A Black Hole

post.title: What happens if you fall into a black hole? 🕳️
post.description:
Send this to a friend who would definitely jump 🫣

Near a black hole, gravity slows time. Outside observers see a falling object freeze and fade at the edge, while the falling person keeps falling.
post.pinned_comment: Would you jump? Yes or no 👇

scenes.narration: If you fell into a black hole, your friends would watch you freeze. Forever.
Let's say you jump. At first, nothing feels strange. You are just falling.
A black hole pulls so hard that not even light can escape. Its edge is called the event horizon.
But gravity also bends time. Near the edge, your clock ticks slower than your friends' clocks far away.
So from far away, they see you slow down, turn red, and fade, frozen at the edge.
But you don't feel frozen at all. If the black hole is small, it pulls on your feet much harder than on your head.
You get stretched into a long, thin noodle. Scientists really call it spaghettification.
But if the black hole is giant, you could cross the edge in one piece, and not even notice.
Once you are inside, there is no way back. Every path you could take leads to the center.
So two stories are true at the same time. Outside, you are frozen forever. Inside, you are still falling.
One person. Two endings. Both real. Would you still jump?
